text:
Sophia: Heads up — support rolled up 3 related tickets asking for streaming support for partial function/tool calls with structured JSON output. Can we triage and decide scope?

Andrew: tickets: #5421, #5478, #5490. Short notes: 1) customer A needs incremental toolcall args while model streams (webhook consumer), 2) customer B wants structured partial records (tabular rows) emitted as they arrive, 3) customer C asks for deterministic framing so proxies can reassemble.

Maria: FYI two of those are enterprise prospects on Dedicated. They expect a QA window in 6 weeks if we can ship a minimal contract. Not ready to promise but want rough ETA.

Leo: Quick feasibility check: streaming fncall + structured output adds complexity: current streaming path sends raw token stream. We need an envelope protocol (frame metadata + payload) and SDK upgrades. Main risks: a) backwards compatibility for existing streaming clients, b) KV-cache/latency regressions when we add framing and JSON emit points.

Jin: Proposed minimal contract (Phase 1): streaming frames are newline-delimited JSON envelopes. Each envelope: {"event":"partial", "kind":"toolcall|record|log", "id":string, "data":object, "final":bool}. Clients can ignore unknown fields. No function-invocation callbacks until schema stable.

Andrew: customers asked for example. Suggest sending this snippet to them to confirm:

```
{"event":"partial","kind":"toolcall","id":"t-123","data":{"name":"lookup","args":{"q":"..."}},"final":false}
{"event":"partial","kind":"record","id":"r-42","data":{"row":["a","b","c"]},"final":false}
{"event":"partial","kind":"record","id":"r-42","data":{"row":["d","e","f"]},"final":true}
```

Sophia: That looks good. Key tradeoffs: supportable quickly vs. long-term semantic fncall streaming. Can we make Phase 1 SDK-friendly so our JS/py clients can expose a frame iterator?

Leo: Yes. Server-side changes: framing serializer, small state machine in streaming path, update SSE and WS connectors. SDK: add .streamFrames() that yields parsed envelopes. Estimate: eng time 3-4 sprints (2 engs) for robust rollout + compatibility tests. If we do a narrower MVP (only 'record' frames, no toolcall), maybe 2 sprints.

Maria: Customers will accept an MVP that streams structured rows only (the sales asks were mostly batch-to-real-time ingestion). If that shortens timeline to land Enterprise deals, mark it P1.

Jin: Launch criteria proposal: 1) server + SDK parsing + docs, 2) contract doc with examples + fallbacks, 3) integration tests against a sample webhook consumer, 4) performance bench showing <10% tail-latency regression for typical seq lengths, 5) security review for payload parsing. Agree?

Andrew: +1. Also need migration instructions for existing streaming clients (how to ignore envelopes).

Leo: Implementation plan: Week 0-1 design & prod doc; Week 2-5 eng work (MVP record frames); Week 6 QA + perf; Week 7 pilot with the two enterprise customers; Week 8 rollout + SDK stable. If we include toolcall streaming, add 2 sprints after pilot.

Sophia: Sounds reasonable. Scope decision: ship MVP that supports 'record' envelopes + framing. Defer toolcall streaming to follow-up unless customers explicitly need live function args (Andrew, confirm).

Andrew: Customer A actually asked for incremental function args. They can accept deferred timeline if we provide a clear roadmap. I'll confirm with them and push demo of the record-MVP.

EVAL-Bot: Perf note: sim load with framing + batch size 8 shows ~6% CPU increase at 95th p95 for 1M token/hour workload.

Sophia: Next steps/actions: 1) Jin to write spec doc and contract PR by EOD Fri @Jin, 2) Leo to scope tickets + estimate story points by Tuesday, 3) Andrew to confirm tooling needs with customer A and share any wire-format constraints, 4) Maria to notify sales that MVP timeline is ~8 weeks and collect pilot participants.

Jin: Will do the spec draft and include example code for JS/py SDK streaming iterator.

Leo: I'll post a tech design doc in #eng-runtime by Monday with proposed serializer and compatibility shim.

Maria: I'll coordinate pilot signups. If customers ask for earlier demo, we can show a strawman local prototype.

Sophia: Great. We'll regroup after the spec PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
